title: No exact continuous PC complete-page extension even for a bounded-relative rational-PA proper-face target
status: FULL4-unit new ROOT working proof, UNREVIEWED

units.statement: Exact rational target already PC on the original partial cells and bounded by its actual reference.
units.proof:
In rational R^3 with coordinates(t,a,b), let e0=(1,0,0), v1=(0,1,0), v2=(0,0,1), v3=(0,-1,-1), sum v_i=0. Full pages V_i=span(e0,v_i) intersect pairwise in H=R e0. On each choose the PROPER rational cell sigma_i={t e0+s v_i:s>=0,0<=u=t+s<=1}, with shared actual face tau=[0,1] e0. Let actual reference gamma_i(t,s)=s and target
f_i(t,s)=max(0,-2t-s)=s+max(-s,-2u).
Both are genuine finite rational-spatial rational-PA functions, convex on each cell, with f_tau=gamma_tau=0. On sigma_i the difference is between -2 and0: max(-s,-2u)>=-2, and max(-s,-2u)<=0. Therefore |f-gamma|<=2 GLOBALLY on the original partial union. The only nonzero recession direction is a positive multiple of(-1,1) in each page; gamma has slope1 there, strictly positive. The target has the same actual recession, also slope1. Each f_i is globally Lipschitz in its rational block l1 norm, with gradient either0 or(-2,-1), so constant2 suffices.

The glued target and reference are continuous printed-PC on this partial support. A legal center outside tau has only its unique page's assigned cells and convex Jensen applies. At a tau-center both values are0 and ALL endpoint values f_i,gamma_i are nonnegative, so every PCC holds, including every inherited lower face. The common ambient p0=0 supports f on ENTIRE sigma_i at EVERYtau point. Use common rational refinements of the line t+s=0,1, s=0 and the f wall2t+s=0; all values/face incidences are genuine and rational.

The original partial support has unbalanced outer facets. It is NOT a globally positive balanced original counterexample; indeed f is already finite PC PA there and has no regularization problem on that support. This is an exact-extension strategy obstruction only.

units.statement: Any continuous printed-PC function on the complete-page book is convex on every entire page; short PCCs control distant page endpoints.
units.proof:
We give the needed implication without assuming the unreviewed native298 theorem. Fix a finite rational carrier for the complete-page book, or a locally finite rational carrier and restrict to compact segments. Each convex inherited cell in a page has real convex restriction: rational endpoints and weights give its rational convex inequalities, and continuity extends them to all real endpoints. A rational segment in the page meets finitely many carrier walls at rational break parameters. At each breakpoint, choose sufficiently short rational endpoints on the two adjacent segment pieces. Their cells share the breakpoint's minimal face, so the printed midpoint/barycentric PCC orders the left and right secants. Combined with convexity inside each piece, every segment secant is monotone across all finitely many breaks, proving convexity on that rational segment. Approximate real endpoints by rational ones in the whole rational page and use continuity to obtain convexity of the function on ENTIRE V_i. No coarsening of the actual carrier is used.

Let y be a rational point of H and z_i=y+v_i be rational endpoints in the pages, with mean y. For sufficiently small rational epsilon>0, every short endpoint y+epsilon v_i lies in some actual carrier cell incident to the minimal face containing y. In a finite/local-finite rational complex, the local tangent cones at y cover each complete page near y; choose epsilon below the finitely many nearby wall distances. The three short endpoints still have mean y, so the legal printed PCC gives
F(y)<= (1/3)sum_i F_i(y+epsilon v_i).
Entire-page convexity bounds each short value by (1-epsilon)F(y)+epsilon F_i(z_i). Canceling yields
F(y)<= (1/3)sum_i F_i(z_i).
The far endpoints need not themselves belong to cells incident to y. The conclusion comes from a genuinely legal SHORT PCC plus entire-page convex secants, not an invalid direct nonincident test. Neither arbitrary raw-PC continuity nor a hidden full-space convex extension is used.

units.statement: Contradictory exact bounds at one rational H point prove NO continuous PC extension, regardless of reference or growth.
units.proof:
Suppose a finite continuous printed-PC F on the COMPLETE union of V1,V2,V3 agrees with f_i on ENTIRE sigma_i. Let y=-e0. The rational original points z_i=-e0+v_i have coordinates(t,s)=(-1,1), u=0, and f_i(z_i)=1. They have mean y. N1's valid short-PCC/secant argument therefore implies F(y)<=1.

In page1 choose the rational interior point q=(t,s)=(-1,3/2), so u=1/2,s=3/2 and -2t-s=1/2>0. In an open neighborhood of this q inside sigma1 the target is the affine function L(t,s)=-2t-s. Exact agreement forces F1=L there. For a finite convex function on the ENTIRE page, an affine piece on an open neighborhood is a global supporting affine form: on the segment q to any x, convex secants are nondecreasing and their initial slope is L_linear(x-q), so F1(x)>=F1(q)+L_linear(x-q)=L(x). Apply this at y=(-1,0) to get F(y)>=L(-1,0)=2.

Thus 2<=F(y)<=1, impossible. There is NO finite continuous printed-PC extension of this already rational-PA, globally Lipschitz, bounded-relative target to the three COMPLETE pages. The contradiction does not require any bounded-difference condition or positive-growth hypothesis on the extension. It therefore holds for any proposed same-reference extension and for any different admitted proper full-book reference.

For a general rational parameter A>1, f_i=max(0,-A t+(1-A)s)=s+max(-s,-A u) has |f-gamma|<=A, shares zero tau trace, positive recession1 and common p0=0, and the same argument gives F(-e0)>=A while F(-e0)<=1. The fixed A=2 case suffices and has only rational constants/points. No finite numeric experiment substitutes for the continuum convexity/PCC argument.

units.statement: Precise significance for the affine-reference extension and original general regularization task.
units.proof:
Working301 gives a constructive compatible positive-growth finite REAL PA reference Gamma on the complete-page book, agreeing with gamma_i=s on each original sigma_i. The present obstruction is consistent: exact AFFINE reference data can extend, while even a bounded-relative continuous rational-PA convex target may have NO exact continuous PC extension. In N2 the affine supporting trace extrapolated from a target's interior has slope-2 on H, which contradicts the remote endpoint upper bound forced by the dependent relation sum v_i=0. This is the exact nonlinear trace obstruction left explicitly open in working301 and cannot be repaired solely by choosing a better reference or a larger norm.

Consequently one cannot obtain arbitrary all-face regularization by first extending every cellwise target exactly to complete affine pages and then applying a complete-book approximation theorem. Direct approximation on the ORIGINAL complex, with genuine face values/supports preserved, or a different approximate-extension mechanism is required. This theorem does not refute such direct regularization. It does not give an original globally balanced counterexample: the partial sigma support omits boundary balancing and the original target is already PA PC. It also does not claim an obstruction for independent quotient normal spaces or for every partial-book geometry.
